CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Billy is a 74-year-old male who presents with a cough that began approximately one week ago. He reports productive cough with yellow sputum and states symptoms have worsened over the past two days. He reports feeling warm but denies having taken his temperature. Denies fever, chills, or shortness of breath. Reports generalized achiness. Additionally, reports nasal congestion with postnasal drainage and sinus pressure. No other household members are ill. Patient works as a teacher. This morning while coughing, the patient fell down approximately 4-5 stairs and twisted his right knee. He reports right knee pain, predominantly on the medial aspect, and has a slight limp but is able to walk. Denies knee giving out. Able to bend and straighten knee. Has been taking over-the-counter Dayquil for cough and cold symptoms with minimal relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for cough with yellow sputum, nasal congestion, postnasal drainage, sinus pressure, and right knee pain. Negative for fever, chills, and shortness of breath.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily
2. Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
3. Over-the-counter Dayquil

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works as a teacher. Lives with wife who assists with medication management. Denies being a sports fan.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Temperature 98.4°F, Blood Pressure 125/62 mmHg, Heart Rate in 80s, Oxygen Saturation 97% on room air
Facial Exam: Pain to palpation over bilateral maxillary sinuses
Nasal Exam: Erythema and edema of nasal turbinates bilaterally with yellow discharge
Oropharyngeal Exam: Uvula midline, no erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space
Neck Exam: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy
Pulmonary Exam: Coarse rhonchi present bilaterally, clears with cough
Cardiac Exam: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur
Right Knee Exam: Pain to palpation, decreased flexion and extension, ecchymosis over right medial knee, no effusion

RESULTS
Laboratory tests and imaging ordered; results pending.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Viral syndrome with mild bronchitis: Continue supportive care and over-the-counter medications. Prescribed guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily. No antibiotics at this time. Patient to call if symptoms worsen; will consider chest x-ray to rule out pneumonia if symptoms progress.

2. Right medial collateral ligament strain from fall: Prescribed meloxicam 15 mg once daily. Referred to physical therapy for strengthening. Right knee x-ray ordered to rule out bony injury.

3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Lipid panel ordered. Patient counseled on blood pressure monitoring and salt restriction.

4. Diabetes mellitus: Continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Hemoglobin A1c ordered. Patient counseled to monitor sugar intake and report blood glucose readings through patient portal.
